records.change: "the Lord said" becomes "And he"
records.note: The Vulgate reads Et ille, as do Sinaiticus and Vaticanus (ho de); the Textus Receptus has "the Lord said". The speaker is still Jesus, who names himself.

records.change: "preached Christ" becomes "preached Jesus"
records.note: The Vulgate reads Jesum, as do Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; the Textus Receptus has "Christ". He still preaches that Jesus is the Son of God.

records.change: Omits the address "Lord"
records.note: The Vulgate has Absit Domine ("Not so, Lord"); the Douay-Rheims renders it "Far be it from me" without the address. A translation choice, not a textual difference.

records.change: Omits "I was fasting"
records.note: The Vulgate reads orans eram (I was praying), as do Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; the Textus Receptus has "fasting" as well as praying. Fasting is still commended elsewhere, as in 13:2-3.

records.change: "before God… of God" becomes "in thy sight… by the Lord"
records.note: The Vulgate reads in conspectu tuo and a Domino; the Textus Receptus has "before God" and "of God". Cornelius and his household still wait to hear what God has commanded.

records.change: "word of God" becomes "word of the Lord"
records.note: The Vulgate reads verbum Domini; the Greek of the Textus Receptus has tou theou (of God). The same divine person is meant; only the title differs.

records.change: "ordained them elders" becomes "ordained to them priests"
records.note: The Douay-Rheims renders the Vulgate's presbyteros (Greek presbyterous, elders) as "priests", the English word that comes from presbyter; the KJV has "elders". A translation choice: Catholic readers see the ordained priesthood here, Protestant readers church elders.

records.change: "Known unto God are all his works" becomes a shorter sentence
records.note: The Vulgate has a shorter form, notum a saeculo est Domino opus suum; Sinaiticus and Vaticanus join a shorter form to verse 17. The Textus Receptus has the fuller sentence.

records.change: Omits "Ye must be circumcised, and keep the law"
records.note: The clause is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus. The issue is stated in verses 1 and 5.

records.change: Adds "and Judas alone departed to Jerusalem"
records.note: The Vulgate keeps the verse, as the KJV does, and adds this clause, found in Codex Bezae; Sinaiticus and Vaticanus lack the whole verse.

records.change: "the Lord had called us" becomes "God had called us"
records.note: The Vulgate reads Deus, as do Sinaiticus and Vaticanus (ho theos); the Textus Receptus has "the Lord".

records.change: "the Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "the Lord Jesus"
records.note: "Christ" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus. Salvation by believing on the Lord Jesus is unchanged.

records.change: "of one blood" becomes "of one"
records.note: The Vulgate reads ex uno, as do Sinaiticus and Vaticanus (ex henos); the Textus Receptus has "one blood". The unity of mankind from one origin is the same.

records.change: "seek the Lord" becomes "seek God"
records.note: The Vulgate reads Deum, as do Sinaiticus and Vaticanus (ton theon); the Textus Receptus has "the Lord".

records.change: "repent" becomes "do penance"
records.note: The Douay-Rheims renders the Vulgate's paenitentiam agite (Greek metanoeite) "do penance" where the KJV has "repent". A translation choice: Catholic usage takes it to include works of penance, Protestant readers a turning of mind and heart.

records.change: "pressed in the spirit" becomes "earnest in preaching"
records.note: The Vulgate reads instabat verbo (pressed on with the word), as do Sinaiticus and Vaticanus (logo); the Textus Receptus has pneumati (in the spirit).

records.change: Omits "I must by all means keep this feast… in Jerusalem"
records.note: The sentence is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus. Paul still promises to return, God willing.

records.change: "the things of the Lord" becomes "the things… of Jesus"
records.note: The Vulgate reads ea quae sunt Jesu, as do Sinaiticus and Vaticanus (peri tou Iesou); the Textus Receptus has "of the Lord". Both refer to Jesus.

records.change: "way of God" becomes "way of the Lord"
records.note: The Vulgate reads viam Domini; the Greek of the Textus Receptus has ten tou theou hodon (the way of God). The same divine person is meant; only the title differs.

records.change: Omits "through grace"
records.note: The Vulgate reads his qui crediderant (them who had believed) without "through grace"; the Greek has dia tes charitos. Salvation by grace is still stated in 15:11.

records.change: "Christ Jesus" becomes "Jesus"
records.note: "Christ" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus. He is still the one John said would come.

records.change: "the Lord Jesus" becomes "the Lord"
records.note: "Jesus" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

records.change: "glorified the Lord" becomes "glorified God"
records.note: The Vulgate reads Deum, as do Sinaiticus and Vaticanus (ton theon); the Textus Receptus has "the Lord".

records.change: "zealous toward God" becomes "zealous for the law"
records.note: The Vulgate reads aemulator legis; the Greek has zelotes tou theou (zealous for God). Paul's zeal is for the law of God either way.

records.change: "the name of the Lord" becomes "his name"
records.note: The Vulgate reads nomine ipsius, as do Sinaiticus and Vaticanus (autou); the Textus Receptus has "of the Lord". The name is of the Just One of verse 14.

records.change: Omits "let us not fight against God"
records.note: The clause is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus. The sentence is left as a question.

records.change: "the God of my fathers" becomes "the Father and my God"
records.note: The Vulgate reads Patri et Deo meo, apparently reading the Greek patroo theo (ancestral God) as "Father and God". Paul's service of the God of Israel is the same.

records.change: "repent… meet for repentance" becomes "do penance… worthy of penance"
records.note: The Douay-Rheims renders the Vulgate's paenitentiam agite (Greek metanoeite) "do penance" where the KJV has "repent". A translation choice: Catholic usage takes it to include works of penance, Protestant readers a turning of mind and heart.

records.change: Omits the centurion delivering the prisoners to the captain
records.note: The clause is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus. Paul is still allowed to live alone with a soldier.

records.change: "the gospel of Christ" becomes "the gospel"
records.note: "Of Christ" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus. The gospel meant is the same.

records.change: "for that all have sinned" becomes "in whom all have sinned"
records.note: The Vulgate reads in quo omnes peccaverunt, taking the Greek eph' ho as "in whom" (in Adam); the KJV has "for that" (because). Augustine built the doctrine of original sin partly on the Latin reading; the passage teaches sin through Adam in both.

records.change: Omits "but after the Spirit"
records.note: The Vulgate has only qui non secundum carnem ambulant; Sinaiticus and Vaticanus have neither clause; the Textus Receptus has both, as in verse 4.

records.change: "word of God" becomes "word of Christ"
records.note: The Vulgate reads verbum Christi, as do Sinaiticus and Vaticanus (rhematos Christou); the Textus Receptus has theou (God).

records.change: Omits "But if it be of works… work is no more work"
records.note: The second half of the verse is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus. Its point is the converse of the first half, which remains: grace excludes works.

records.change: Omits "he that regardeth not the day" clause
records.note: The clause is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus. The parallel clause about eating is kept.

records.change: "the Spirit of God" becomes "the Holy Ghost"
records.note: The Vulgate reads Spiritus Sancti, with some Greek manuscripts; the Textus Receptus has "Spirit of God". The same Spirit is meant.

records.change: "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Christ our Lord"
records.note: "Jesus" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

records.change: Omits the closing "Amen"
records.note: The "Amen" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus. The meaning is unchanged.

records.change: Omits the subscription "Written to the Romans from Corinthus…"
records.note: The subscription is a later note found in the Textus Receptus and printed by the KJV; it is not in the Vulgate or the earliest Greek manuscripts and is not part of the text.

records.change: "testimony of God" becomes "testimony of Christ"
records.note: The Vulgate reads testimonium Christi, with some Greek manuscripts; the Textus Receptus has "of God", and some early manuscripts "mystery of God".

records.change: "the Holy Ghost teacheth" becomes "the doctrine of the Spirit"
records.note: "Holy" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus. The Spirit meant is the same.

records.change: Second "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "our Lord Jesus"
records.note: The second "Christ" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

records.change: Omits "and in your spirit, which are God's"; adds "and bear"
records.note: The Vulgate reads glorificate et portate Deum in corpore vestro; Sinaiticus and Vaticanus also lack the clause about the spirit, which is in the Textus Receptus. "Bear God" is a Latin addition.

records.change: Omits "fasting"
records.note: "Fasting" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus. Only prayer is named as the reason for abstaining.

records.change: "please the Lord" becomes "please God"
records.note: The Vulgate reads placeat Deo; the Greek of the Textus Receptus has kyrio (the Lord). The same divine person is meant; only the title differs.

records.change: "a sister, a wife" becomes "a woman, a sister"
records.note: The Greek adelphen gynaika can mean "a sister as wife" or "a sister, a woman"; the Vulgate's mulierem sororem is read by Catholics of a woman helper, the KJV's "a sister, a wife" of a believing wife, as Peter had (Matthew 8:14).

records.change: "the gospel of Christ" becomes "the gospel"
records.note: "Of Christ" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

records.change: "body of Christ" becomes "body of the Lord"
records.note: The Vulgate reads corporis Domini; the Greek of the Textus Receptus has tou Christou (of Christ). The same divine person is meant; only the title differs.

records.change: Omits "for the earth is the Lord's, and the fulness thereof"
records.note: The repeated quotation of Psalm 24:1 is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus. It stands in verse 26.

records.change: "broken for you" becomes "delivered for you"
records.note: The Vulgate reads quod pro vobis tradetur (which shall be delivered); Sinaiticus and Vaticanus have only "which is for you"; the Textus Receptus has klomenon (broken).

records.change: "eat this bread, and drink this cup" becomes "or drink the chalice"
records.note: The Vulgate reads vel biberit (or drink), as do most Greek manuscripts (e); the Textus Receptus has kai (and). The Catholic practice of communion in one kind has been linked to this reading.

records.change: "the Lord from heaven" becomes "from heaven, heavenly"
records.note: The Vulgate reads secundus homo de caelo, caelestis; Sinaiticus and Vaticanus have "from heaven" without "the Lord", which is in the Textus Receptus. Christ's heavenly origin is still stated.

records.change: "We shall not all sleep" becomes "We shall all indeed rise again"
records.note: The Vulgate reads omnes quidem resurgemus, sed non omnes immutabimur, from a Greek variant (in Bezae); the Textus Receptus and most manuscripts have "we shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed". Both teach the resurrection and transformation at the last trumpet.

records.change: Omits the subscription "written from Philippi…"
records.note: The subscription is a later note found in the Textus Receptus and printed by the KJV; it is not in the Vulgate or the earliest Greek manuscripts and is not part of the text.

records.change: "the Lord Jesus" becomes "Jesus"
records.note: "The Lord" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

records.change: "raised up the Lord Jesus" becomes "raised up Jesus"
records.note: The Vulgate reads suscitavit Jesum and cum Jesu (with Jesus), as do Vaticanus and some others; the Textus Receptus has "the Lord Jesus" and "by Jesus".

records.change: "by Jesus Christ" becomes "by Christ"
records.note: "Jesus" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

records.change: "in the sight of the Lord" becomes "before God"
records.note: The Vulgate reads coram Deo; the Greek of the Textus Receptus has kyriou (the Lord). The same divine person is meant; only the title differs.

records.change: "thanksgivings unto God" becomes "thanksgivings in the Lord"
records.note: The Vulgate reads in Domino; the Greek of the Textus Receptus has to theo (to God). The same divine person is meant; only the title differs.

records.change: "whom the Lord commendeth" becomes "whom God commendeth"
records.note: The Vulgate reads Deus; the Greek of the Textus Receptus has ho kyrios (the Lord). The same divine person is meant; only the title differs.

records.change: "another Jesus" becomes "another Christ"
records.note: The Vulgate reads alium Christum; the Greek has allon Iesoun (another Jesus). The warning against a false gospel is the same.

records.change: "after the Lord" becomes "according to God"
records.note: The Vulgate reads secundum Deum; the Greek of the Textus Receptus has kata kyrion (after the Lord). The same divine person is meant; only the title differs.

records.change: Omits the second "lest I should be exalted above measure"
records.note: The Vulgate states the purpose once; the Greek, both the Textus Receptus and most manuscripts, repeats it at the end of the verse. The meaning is the same.

records.change: Omits the subscription "written from Philippi…"
records.note: The subscription is a later note found in the Textus Receptus and printed by the KJV; it is not in the Vulgate or the earliest Greek manuscripts and is not part of the text.

records.change: "it pleased God" becomes "it pleased him"
records.note: The Vulgate reads placuit ei, as do Vaticanus and some others; the Textus Receptus names God. The one who called Paul is plainly God.

records.change: Omits "in Christ" after "confirmed before of God"
records.note: "In Christ" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

records.change: "heir of God through Christ" becomes "heir also through God"
records.note: The Vulgate reads haeres per Deum, as do Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; the Textus Receptus has "of God through Christ".

records.change: Omits the subscription "To the Galatians written from Rome"
records.note: The subscription is a later note found in the Textus Receptus and printed by the KJV; it is not in the Vulgate or the earliest Greek manuscripts and is not part of the text.

records.change: Omits "by Jesus Christ" after "created all things"
records.note: "By Jesus Christ" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus. Christ's part in creation is still stated in Colossians 1:16 and John 1:3.

records.change: "fruit of the Spirit" becomes "fruit of the light"
records.note: The Vulgate reads fructus lucis, as do Sinaiticus and Vaticanus (photos); the Textus Receptus has pneumatos (Spirit), as in Galatians 5:22.

records.change: "acceptable unto the Lord" becomes "well pleasing to God"
records.note: The Vulgate reads beneplacitum Deo; the Greek of the Textus Receptus has to kyrio (unto the Lord). The same divine person is meant; only the title differs.

records.change: "the will of the Lord" becomes "the will of God"
records.note: The Vulgate reads voluntas Dei; the Greek of the Textus Receptus has tou kyriou (of the Lord). The same divine person is meant; only the title differs.

records.change: "fear of God" becomes "fear of Christ"
records.note: The Vulgate reads timore Christi, as do Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; the Textus Receptus has theou (God).

records.change: "the Lord" becomes "Christ"
records.note: The Vulgate reads Christus, as do Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; the Textus Receptus has ho kyrios (the Lord). Both refer to Christ.

records.change: "a great mystery" becomes "a great sacrament"
records.note: The Vulgate renders the Greek mysterion as sacramentum, which the Douay-Rheims gives as "sacrament"; the KJV has "mystery". Catholic teaching counts marriage a sacrament partly from this verse; the passage speaks of Christ and the church in both.

records.change: Omits the subscription "To the Ephesians written from Rome…"
records.note: The subscription is a later note found in the Textus Receptus and printed by the KJV; it is not in the Vulgate or the earliest Greek manuscripts and is not part of the text.

records.change: "partakers of my grace" becomes "partakers of my joy"
records.note: The Vulgate reads socios gaudii mei; the Greek has charitos (grace). A Latin reading, perhaps of chara (joy) for charis.

records.change: Verses 16 and 17 are in the reverse order
records.note: The Vulgate puts "some out of charity" before "some out of contention", as do Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; the Textus Receptus has the reverse. The content is the same.

records.change: "through Christ" becomes "in him"
records.note: The Vulgate reads in eo, as do Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; the Textus Receptus names Christ. The one who strengthens is plainly Christ.

records.change: "with you all" becomes "with your spirit"; omits the subscription
records.note: The Vulgate reads cum spiritu vestro, as do the early Greek manuscripts. The subscription is a later note found in the Textus Receptus and printed by the KJV; it is not in the Vulgate or the earliest Greek manuscripts and is not part of the text.

records.change: "worthy of the Lord" becomes "worthy of God"
records.note: The Vulgate reads digne Deo; the Greek of the Textus Receptus has tou kyriou (of the Lord). The same divine person is meant; only the title differs.

records.change: "Christ forgave" becomes "the Lord hath forgiven"
records.note: The Vulgate reads Dominus, as do Vaticanus and some others (ho kyrios); the Textus Receptus has ho Christos. Both refer to Christ.

records.change: "peace of God" becomes "peace of Christ"
records.note: The Vulgate reads pax Christi, as do Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; the Textus Receptus has tou theou (of God).

records.change: "to the Lord" becomes "to God"
records.note: The Vulgate reads Deo, as do Sinaiticus and Vaticanus (to theo); the Textus Receptus has to kyrio (to the Lord).

records.change: Omits "from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ"
records.note: The second half of the greeting is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus. The Douay-Rheims has only "Grace be to you and peace", at the start of its verse 2.

records.change: "to meet the Lord" becomes "to meet Christ"
records.note: The Vulgate reads obviam Christo; the Greek has tou kyriou (the Lord). The Lord meant is Christ in both.

records.change: Omits the subscription "written from Athens"
records.note: The subscription is a later note found in the Textus Receptus and printed by the KJV; it is not in the Vulgate or the earliest Greek manuscripts and is not part of the text.

records.change: "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "our Lord Jesus"
records.note: The Douay-Rheims omits "Christ" in the first phrase, as do Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; the Clementine Vulgate and the Textus Receptus have it.

records.change: "day of Christ" becomes "day of the Lord"
records.note: The Vulgate reads dies Domini, as do Sinaiticus and Vaticanus (tou kyriou); the Textus Receptus has tou Christou.

records.change: Omits "as God" before "sitteth in the temple"
records.note: "As God" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus. He still shows himself as if he were God.

records.change: "beloved of the Lord" becomes "of God"; "from the beginning" becomes "firstfruits"
records.note: The Vulgate reads dilecti a Deo and primitias (firstfruits), the latter as Vaticanus (aparchen); the Textus Receptus has kyriou and ap' arches (from the beginning).

records.change: "word of the Lord" becomes "word of God"
records.note: The Vulgate reads sermo Dei; the Greek of the Textus Receptus has tou kyriou (of the Lord). The same divine person is meant; only the title differs.

records.change: "the Lord is faithful" becomes "God is faithful"
records.note: The Vulgate reads Deus; the Greek of the Textus Receptus has ho kyrios (the Lord). The same divine person is meant; only the title differs.

records.change: Omits the subscription "written from Athens"
records.note: The subscription is a later note found in the Textus Receptus and printed by the KJV; it is not in the Vulgate or the earliest Greek manuscripts and is not part of the text.

records.change: "Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Christ Jesus"
records.note: "Lord" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

records.change: Omits "in Christ" from "I speak the truth"
records.note: "In Christ" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

records.change: "God was manifest" becomes "which was manifested"
records.note: The Vulgate reads quod manifestatum est (which was manifested), with the Western Greek ho; Sinaiticus has hos (who), the Textus Receptus theos (God). Christ's deity is stated elsewhere, as in John 1:1 and Titus 2:13.

records.change: Omits "in spirit" from the list
records.note: "In spirit" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

records.change: "the presbytery" becomes "the priesthood"; "gift" becomes "grace"
records.note: The Douay-Rheims renders the Vulgate's presbyterii (Greek presbyteriou, body of elders) as "priests", the English word that comes from presbyter; the KJV has "elders". A translation choice: Catholic readers see the ordained priesthood here, Protestant readers church elders.

records.change: "the Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Christ Jesus"
records.note: "Lord" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

records.change: "name of God" becomes "name of the Lord"
records.note: The Vulgate reads nomen Domini; the Greek of the Textus Receptus has tou theou (of God). The same divine person is meant; only the title differs.

records.change: Omits "from such withdraw thyself"
records.note: The clause is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus. Verse 11 still tells Timothy to flee these things.

records.change: Omits the subscription "written from Laodicea…"
records.note: The subscription is a later note found in the Textus Receptus and printed by the KJV; it is not in the Vulgate or the earliest Greek manuscripts and is not part of the text.

records.change: "name of Christ" becomes "name of the Lord"
records.note: The Vulgate reads nomen Domini, as do Sinaiticus and Vaticanus (kyriou); the Textus Receptus has Christou.

records.change: "the Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Jesus Christ"
records.note: "The Lord" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

records.change: Omits the subscription "ordained the first bishop…"
records.note: The subscription is a later note found in the Textus Receptus and printed by the KJV; it is not in the Vulgate or the earliest Greek manuscripts and is not part of the text.

records.change: Omits "mercy"; "the Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Christ Jesus"
records.note: "Mercy" and "Lord" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

records.change: "ordain elders" becomes "ordain priests"
records.note: The Douay-Rheims renders the Vulgate's presbyteros (Greek presbyterous, elders) as "priests", the English word that comes from presbyter; the KJV has "elders". A translation choice: Catholic readers see the ordained priesthood here, Protestant readers church elders.

records.change: "that bringeth salvation" becomes "God our Saviour"
records.note: The Vulgate reads gratia Dei Salvatoris nostri; the Greek has he soterios (bringing salvation). The grace still saves; the Vulgate names God as Saviour.

records.change: Omits the subscription "ordained the first bishop…"
records.note: The subscription is a later note found in the Textus Receptus and printed by the KJV; it is not in the Vulgate or the earliest Greek manuscripts and is not part of the text.

records.change: Omits the subscription "Written from Rome to Philemon…"
records.note: The subscription is a later note found in the Textus Receptus and printed by the KJV; it is not in the Vulgate or the earliest Greek manuscripts and is not part of the text.

records.change: Omits "by himself" and "our" from purging sins
records.note: The Vulgate reads purgationem peccatorum faciens, as do Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; the Textus Receptus has di' heautou (by himself) and hemon (our). Christ still makes the purification of sins.

records.change: "Christ Jesus" becomes "Jesus"
records.note: "Christ" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

records.change: "the eternal Spirit" becomes "the Holy Ghost"
records.note: The Vulgate reads per Spiritum Sanctum, with a few Greek manuscripts (hagiou); the Textus Receptus and most have aioniou (eternal). Both may be read as the Holy Spirit.

records.change: "Christ is not entered" becomes "Jesus is not entered"
records.note: The Vulgate reads Jesus; the Greek has ho Christos. The same person is meant.

records.change: "blood of Jesus" becomes "blood of Christ"
records.note: The Vulgate reads sanguine Christi; the Greek has Iesou. The atoning blood is the same.

records.change: Omits "saith the Lord"
records.note: "Saith the Lord" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus. The next quotation still names the Lord.

records.change: "me in my bonds" becomes "them in bands"; omits "in heaven"
records.note: The Vulgate reads vinctis (the prisoners), as do the early manuscripts (desmiois), and lacks "in heaven", with Sinaiticus and others; the Textus Receptus has desmois mou and en ouranois.

records.change: "worshipped, leaning upon" becomes "adored the top of his rod"
records.note: The Greek, quoting the Septuagint of Genesis 47:31, is prosekynesen epi to akron tes rhabdou autou; the Vulgate reads adoravit fastigium virgae ejus, as if Jacob venerated the staff, the KJV supplies "leaning" so that he worshipped God upon it.

records.change: "see the Lord" becomes "see God"
records.note: The Vulgate reads videbit Deum; the Greek of the Textus Receptus has ton kyrion (the Lord). The same divine person is meant; only the title differs.

records.change: Omits the subscription "Written to the Hebrews from Italy…"
records.note: The subscription is a later note found in the Textus Receptus and printed by the KJV; it is not in the Vulgate or the earliest Greek manuscripts and is not part of the text.

records.change: "the Lord hath promised" becomes "God hath promised"
records.note: The Vulgate reads Deus; the Textus Receptus has ho kyrios, and Sinaiticus and Vaticanus only the verb.

records.change: "the elders of the church" becomes "the priests of the church"
records.note: The Douay-Rheims renders the Vulgate's presbyteros (Greek presbyterous, elders) as "priests", the English word that comes from presbyter; the KJV has "elders". A translation choice: Catholic readers see the ordained priesthood here, Protestant readers church elders. Catholic teaching finds the anointing of the sick here.

records.change: Omits "through the Spirit"
records.note: "Through the Spirit" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus. The Vulgate also reads "obedience of charity" for "obeying the truth".

records.change: Adds "unto salvation"
records.note: The Vulgate reads crescatis in salutem, as do Sinaiticus and Vaticanus (eis soterian); the Textus Receptus lacks the phrase.

records.change: "for the Lord's sake" becomes "for God's sake"
records.note: The Vulgate reads propter Deum; the Greek of the Textus Receptus has dia ton kyrion (for the Lord's sake). The same divine person is meant; only the title differs.

records.change: "the Lord God" becomes "the Lord Christ"
records.note: The Vulgate reads Dominum Christum, as do Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; the Textus Receptus has kyrion ton theon. Applied to Isaiah 8:13, the Vulgate's reading calls Christ the LORD to be sanctified.

records.change: Omits "for us"
records.note: "For us" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus. Christ's suffering for sins is stated in 3:18.

records.change: "God's heritage" becomes "the clergy"
records.note: The Greek ton kleron (the portions allotted) is rendered from the Vulgate's in cleris as "the clergy"; the KJV supplies "God's heritage", the people in the elders' charge. A translation choice.

records.change: Adds "by good works" to making your calling sure
records.note: The Vulgate reads per bona opera, with a few Greek manuscripts (Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus: dia ton kalon ergon); the Textus Receptus lacks the phrase. Verses 5-8 already call for virtue added to faith.

records.change: Omits "before the Lord"
records.note: The Vulgate lacks "before the Lord", as do Alexandrinus and some others; the Textus Receptus and Sinaiticus and Vaticanus have para kyrio.

records.change: Omits "for ever" from the reserved darkness
records.note: "For ever" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus. The darkness is still reserved for them.

records.change: "day of God" becomes "day of the Lord"
records.note: The Vulgate reads diei Domini; the Greek of the Textus Receptus has tes tou theou hemeras (the day of God). The same divine person is meant; only the title differs.

records.change: "confesseth not that Jesus Christ is come…" becomes "dissolveth Jesus"
records.note: The Vulgate reads qui solvit Jesum (that dissolves, or divides, Jesus), from a Greek variant lyei known to early writers; the Textus Receptus has the fuller confession, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus "confesseth not Jesus". The incarnation is still confessed in verse 2.

records.change: "the Spirit is truth" becomes "Christ is the truth"
records.note: The Vulgate reads quoniam Christus est veritas; the Greek has hoti to pneuma estin he aletheia (the Spirit is truth). The Spirit still testifies.

records.change: Omits "and that ye may believe on the name…"
records.note: The last clause is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus. The verse still addresses those who believe in the name of the Son of God.

records.change: "begotten of God keepeth himself" becomes "generation of God preserveth him"
records.note: The Vulgate reads generatio Dei conservat eum, taking the Greek ho gennetheis (he that was begotten) as the begetting itself, and "him" with Vaticanus (auton). Either way the one born of God is kept from the evil one.

records.change: Omits "Jesus Christ"; "him that is true" becomes "the true God"
records.note: The Vulgate reads ut cognoscamus verum Deum et simus in vero Filio ejus, without the name; the Greek has "him that is true… in his Son Jesus Christ". The verse still ends "This is the true God".

records.change: "the Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Christ Jesus"
records.note: "The Lord" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

records.change: Second "doctrine of Christ" becomes "the doctrine"
records.note: The second "of Christ" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus. The Vulgate also reads recedit (revolteth) for "transgresseth".

records.change: Omits the closing "Amen"
records.note: The closing "Amen" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

records.change: "the only Lord God" becomes "the only sovereign Ruler"
records.note: The Vulgate reads solum Dominatorem without Deum, as do Sinaiticus and Vaticanus (despoten without theon); the Textus Receptus has "the only Lord God". Whether one or two persons are meant depends on this word.

records.change: "the Lord" becomes "Jesus" as saviour of Israel from Egypt
records.note: The Vulgate reads Jesus, as do Alexandrinus and Vaticanus; the Textus Receptus has ho kyrios. The Vulgate's reading makes Jesus the one who brought Israel out of Egypt.

records.change: Omits "wise"; adds "through Jesus Christ our Lord"
records.note: The Vulgate reads soli Deo Salvatori nostro, per Jesum Christum Dominum nostrum, and "before all ages", as do Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; the Textus Receptus has "only wise God" and lacks the rest.

records.change: "saith the Lord" becomes "saith the Lord God"
records.note: The Vulgate reads Dominus Deus, as do the early Greek manuscripts; the Textus Receptus has ho kyrios. The Vulgate keeps "the beginning and the end", which Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus lack.

records.change: Omits "Christ" twice after "Jesus"
records.note: The Vulgate reads in Christo Jesu and testimonium Jesu, as do Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus in part; the Textus Receptus has "Jesus Christ" twice.

records.change: Omits "I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last"
records.note: The self-description is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus. Christ still calls himself the First and the Last in verse 17.

records.change: Omits "Amen"; "hell and death" become "death and hell"
records.note: The Vulgate lacks "Amen" and has mortis et inferni, as do the early Greek manuscripts; the Textus Receptus has "Amen" and hell before death.

records.change: "repent" becomes "do penance" twice
records.note: The Douay-Rheims renders the Vulgate's paenitentiam agite (Greek metanoeite) "do penance" where the KJV has "repent". A translation choice: Catholic usage takes it to include works of penance, Protestant readers a turning of mind and heart.

records.change: Adds "in Latin Exterminans" to Abaddon and Apollyon
records.note: The Vulgate gives the angel's name in Latin as well (latine habens nomen Exterminans, "Destroyer"); the Greek gives only the Hebrew and Greek names. The meaning is the same.

records.change: "repented not" becomes "did not do penance"
records.note: The Douay-Rheims renders the Vulgate's paenitentiam agite (Greek metanoeite) "do penance" where the KJV has "repent". A translation choice: Catholic usage takes it to include works of penance, Protestant readers a turning of mind and heart.

records.change: Omits "the angel stood"
records.note: The Vulgate reads dictum est mihi (it was said to me), as do the early Greek manuscripts; the Textus Receptus has "the angel stood, saying". The command to measure is the same.

records.change: "the God of the earth" becomes "the Lord of the earth"
records.note: The Vulgate reads Domini terrae, as do the early Greek manuscripts (kyriou); the Textus Receptus has theou.

records.change: "Fear God" becomes "Fear the Lord"
records.note: The Vulgate reads Timete Dominum; the Greek of the Textus Receptus has ton theon (God). The same divine person is meant; only the title differs.

records.change: Omits "of heaven" after "temple"
records.note: "Of heaven" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

records.change: "God hath remembered" becomes "the Lord hath remembered"
records.note: The Vulgate reads Dominus; the Greek of the Textus Receptus has ho theos (God). The same divine person is meant; only the title differs.

records.change: "the Lord God" becomes "God"
records.note: The Vulgate reads Deus, as do Alexandrinus and some others; the Textus Receptus has kyrios ho theos.

records.change: Omits "honour" and "the Lord"
records.note: "Honour" and "the Lord" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Vulgate or in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus. The praise is to "our God".

records.change: "stand before God" becomes "before the throne"
records.note: The Vulgate reads in conspectu throni, as do the Greek manuscripts generally; the Textus Receptus has theou (God), from Erasmus's Latin-based text. The judgment is still before God's throne (verse 11).

records.change: Voice "out of heaven" becomes "from the throne"
records.note: The Vulgate reads de throno, as do Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus; the Textus Receptus has ek tou ouranou (out of heaven).

records.change: "do his commandments" becomes "wash their robes in the blood…"
records.note: The Vulgate reads qui lavant stolas suas in sanguine Agni; Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus have "wash their robes" without "in the blood of the Lamb"; the Textus Receptus has "do his commandments". The Lamb's blood washing robes is in 7:14.
